A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, three readable result tables, and matching Appendices A–E. v2 additionally appends an unreferenced mnist.png availability notice and a template title page. The unavailable image cannot be assessed, but it does not prevent reliable comparison of the paper's scientific content.

before.justification: Section 6 and Tables 1–3 report original experiments on graph anomaly detection, Wasserstein distance prediction, and MNIST/CIFAR10 weight-space alignment.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experiments and their results in Section 6 and Tables 1–3, including revised MNIST entries in Table 3.

M1.justification: The irreducible-decomposition approach, SchurNet layers, wreath-equivariant construction, and selected non-Siamese weight-space mappings remain unchanged. The decomposition algorithms in Appendices C and D are also retained.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic graph anomaly task, six Wasserstein datasets, and weight-space alignment on MNIST and CIFAR10. RNAseq becoming RNA-seq is a spelling change; the represented data and test scenarios remain the same.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Siamese and DSS in Table 1, NProductNet in Table 2, and the Siamese weight-space model in Table 3. Updating Navon et al. from its 2023 preprint citation to its 2024 publication does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: The noise levels, input sizes, same-size versus different-size Wasserstein tests, metrics, and model-selection procedures are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same architecture details and training budgets, including 100 epochs for alignment and 200 for Wasserstein prediction.

E4.justification: Both retain the graph-noise comparison in Table 1 and the set-size generalization tests in Table 2. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is added or removed from the matched main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. The unchanged searches over hyperparameter configurations are not reported as statistical repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 3 exchanges the MNIST Acc(↓) values: SchurNet changes from 1.5e-5 to 1.25e-5, while Siamese changes from 1.25e-5 to 1.5e-5, reversing their ranking under the same reported settings. The PDFs do not explain the revision. Other result values are unchanged apart from equivalent trailing-zero formatting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, decomposition theorems, wreath-product characterization, and proofs in Appendices B–E are unchanged. Adding the Poonen citation supports an existing statement about real representations rather than revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: alternative irreducible-based derivations, simpler weight-space characterization, general wreath-equivariant layers, and empirical benefits from non-Siamese layers. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of Siamese failure, the rationale for selecting fewer weight-space mappings, applicability qualifications, and proposed higher-order graph extensions remain unchanged. The claim of outperforming the alignment baseline in all settings is retained despite the Table 3 revision.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies the same optimizers, hyperparameter searches, layer widths, epoch budgets, learning rate, and weight decay. Both versions provide the same GitHub code link; no new implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds Poonen's Real representations (2016), replacing an unresolved citation in Section 3. Navon and Wang references receive publication-metadata updates, while the related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence remain essentially identical. Limited editorial changes include bibliographic cleanup, revised table captions, an added funding acknowledgment, and omission of the extraneous template title page.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 are reformatted from compact wrapped tables into centered displays. Table 2 moves to page 10, gains runner-up underlining and an explanatory caption, and avoids v2's footer overlap and clipped caption. The trailing image notice and template page disappear, while stray code-fence text appears on v4 page 9; no scientific figure deletion is established.

improvement.justification: v4 improves table readability, particularly by fixing Table 2's placement, and resolves the missing Section 3 citation. The revised Table 3 agrees with the retained ranking claim, although the exchanged values are unexplained and do not establish new validation. These limited clarity and consistency gains outweigh the small formatting regression on page 9; the scientific contribution and supporting analyses remain essentially unchanged.
